html:
Modu was the founder of the Xiongnu empire, the first great empire of the steppe nomads, on the plains of Mongolia. He ruled from 209 to 174 BCE.

The Chinese historian Sima Qian tells how he took power. Modu trained his men to shoot wherever his whistling arrow flew, and killed those who did not. He shot at his favourite horse, then at his wife, and finally at his father, the chanyu Touman. His men followed, and Modu became ruler.

He then united the tribes of the grasslands. He crushed the Donghu to the east and drove the Yuezhi from the west, a move that later pushed them toward Bactria.

In 200 BCE he trapped the founder of the Han dynasty, Emperor Gaozu, at Baideng. The emperor escaped, but the Han then signed the heqin treaties: they sent princesses as brides and yearly gifts of silk, grain and wine in return for peace. The balance of power between steppe and China that Modu set lasted until Emperor Wu of Han went to war decades later.
sum: Modu was the founder of the Xiongnu empire, the first great empire of the steppe nomads, on the plains of Mongolia. He ruled from 209 to 174 BCE.
